title: Quasi-isomorphism comparison for telescopes of truncation replacements

source.place: Proof of Lemma 06YS, via Lemma 077J; Derived Categories, Lemma 0949

from.place: The existence of a K-flat resolution: compatible bounded-above replacements and their telescope comparison

lean.statement: theorem quasiIso_flat_truncation_telescope {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (E : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1)) (q : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ G.truncLE (n : ℤ)) (hq : ∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (q n)) (hcompat : ∀ n : ℕ, t n ≫ q (n + 1) ≫ G.ιTruncLE ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = q n ≫ G.ιTruncLE (n : ℤ)) (f : mappingCone (𝟙 (∐ E) - Sigma.desc (fun n : ℕ ↦ t n ≫ Sigma.ι E (n + 1))) ⟶ G) (hinr : mappingCone.inr _ ≫ f = Sigma.desc (fun n : ℕ ↦ q n ≫ G.ιTruncLE (n : ℤ))) (hinl : (mappingCone.inl _).comp (HomComplex.Cochain.ofHom f) (add_zero _) = 0) : QuasiIso f

statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $G$ and $E_n$ ($n\in\mathbf N$) be cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with maps $t_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and quasi-isomorphisms $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}G$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Assume $t_n q_{n+1}\iota_{n+1}=q_n\iota_n$, where $\iota_n$ is the good truncation inclusion into $G$. Set $B=\bigoplus_nE_n$ and $\phi=1-\operatorname{shift}_t:B\to B$, with shift given on the $n$th summand by $t_n$ into summand $n+1$. If $f:\operatorname{Cone}(\phi)\to G$ is a chain map whose restriction to the unshifted summand is $\sum_n q_n\iota_n$ and whose restriction to the shifted summand is zero, then $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No flatness, boundedness or epimorphism assumption is imposed on $E_n$ or $q_n$.

proof.text: Use the compatible truncation transition maps and the canonical quasi-isomorphism $g$ from their telescope to $G$ in [lem-pc-kflat-hocolim-truncations]. Since each truncation inclusion is monic, the compatibility after inclusion into $G$ implies that the maps $q_n$ commute with the truncation transitions.

Sheaves of modules form a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], so coproducts are exact. The source-library declaration HomologicalComplex.isStableUnderColimitsOfShape_quasiIso makes the coproduct $\sigma=\bigoplus_n q_n$ a quasi-isomorphism. Compatibility gives a square between the two one-minus-shift maps, with both vertical maps equal to $\sigma$.

The square induces a map of cone triangles. Apply the standard derived localization functor to it. The first two maps are isomorphisms, so Pretriangulated.isIso₃_of_isIso₁₂ makes the map on cones an isomorphism in the derived category, hence a quasi-isomorphism of complexes. The composite with $g$ agrees with $f$ on the shifted and unshifted summands; mapping-cone extensionality identifies them. Composition of quasi-isomorphisms gives the conclusion.
